subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
unit: Across Cultures · Reading for Pleasure · Review and Reference
lesson: Review and Reference: Theme 4 learning objectives and core words test
outcomes: Check your progress on the Theme 4 learning objectives
Spell and use the Theme 4 core words correctly
Use the present perfect and present perfect continuous correctly

tf.s: 'Freight' means goods carried by trains or lorries.
tf.why: Yes, freight is goods that are transported.

tf.s: 'Emit' means to send out something, such as gas.

tf.why: Right, in- makes the opposite of edible.

tf.s: A 'campaign' is a planned set of activities to reach a goal.
tf.why: Yes, like a road safety campaign.

tf.s: 'I've been calling you all morning' uses the present perfect continuous.
'I've known him since 2015' is wrong because we must say 'I know him since 2015'.
tf.why: With since we use the present perfect: I've known him.
Currently means now, at the present time.

tf.s: A 'traffic jam' is a long line of vehicles that cannot move or move very slowly.
tf.why: Yes, traffic jams happen on busy roads.
A flyer is a small printed paper that gives information.

boxes.q: Which word means 'goods carried by trains or lorries'?

boxes.why: Inedible is the opposite of edible.
Conventional fuel is the usual fuel.

boxes.q: Which word means 'at the present time'?
Which word goes with a point in time?
boxes.why: We use since with a starting point, like since 2015.

boxes.q: Which word means 'an advantage or good result'?
boxes.why: A benefit is something good you get.

boxes.q: Which word is another name for a lorry?
boxes.why: A truck carries goods by road.

hunt.q: A large road vehicle for goods

o: a person who is among the first to do something
The police launched a road safety campaign.
I ate a campaign for lunch.
mcq.why: A campaign is a planned set of activities.

mcq.q: Complete: He has ___ (train) for the race for three months.
mcq.why: have/has been + -ing shows an action continuing to now.
Present perfect uses the past participle: known.

o: My car has been getting older, so I've got a new one.
My car have been get older.
My car is been getting older.
mcq.why: has been + -ing is the correct form.

mcq.q: Why do we say 'I've been mending my bike all day' and not 'I mend my bike all day'?
o: the action started in the past and is still continuing
the action is finished long ago
it happens every day as a habit
mcq.why: The present perfect continuous links past and now.

mcq.q: Petrol is called a 'conventional' fuel. What does this suggest?
o: it is the usual fuel most people use
it is a new type of fuel

mcq.q: Which pair of words has opposite meanings?
mcq.why: The prefix in- gives the opposite meaning.
